text:
sam: quick RFC sketch: proposing a 'sparse page map' for paged KV to reduce blocktable scanning during allocation. want early feedback before I write up a full PR
aria: 👀 outline? curious how this differs from slotmap / slab stuff we've discussed
sam: short: keep a compact per-shard page-index that points to live blocks and a small free-run list per page. avoid scanning the whole block table on alloc. allocate inside page first, fall back to page-split.
devin: so page = contiguous KV page (e.g., 64 blocks)? how do we track holes/frags inside a page?
sam: each page has a 16-bit free-run header + a bloom-ish fast-empty bitmap. block entries still in block table but we maintain an index vector of candidate pages ordered by free-run length.
maya: sketch of header please — easier to reason over code
sam: sure, pseudocode snippet:
```
struct PageIndexEntry {
  uint32_t page_id; // base block idx/addr
  uint16_t longest_free_run; // in blocks
  uint16_t free_bitmap_offset; // offset into shared bitmap arena
}
// global: vector<PageIndexEntry> page_index; // kept compact, rebalanced occasionally
```
aria: Hmm. how do we keep page_index updated under high QPS? frequent updates could be a perf sink
sam: plan: epoched updates + write-combining. local thread writes to per-cpu delta, background thread merges into page_index every 50ms. alloc path reads a snapshot.
devin: snapshot reads OK for latency but could lead to over-alloc into pages becoming full. we need a fast local reserve counter per page?
sam: yep — lightweight atomic 'reserved' counter per page used by fast path; only fallback hits global index.
bench-bot: bench run (dev branch + sparse-map opt) 1000 iters, seq len 1024, batch 8:
- baseline paged-KV (slotmap): p95 alloc latency 1.8ms, throughput 1200 req/s
- sparse-page-map: p95 alloc latency 1.1ms, throughput 1580 req/s
- mem overhead +1.7%
ops-bot: noted. did you collect eviction/regression curves?
sam: yes, preliminary eviction churn lower since we avoid scanning blocks for small allocs. eviction rate drop ~18% in that bench. will attach flame next.
maya: what about fragmentation over time? does longest_free_run approach cause page hot spots and long-tail fragmentation?
sam: good point. the index supports periodic compaction: we prefer allocating from pages with largest free runs; when fragmentation crosses threshold we schedule a background compaction pass that migrates hot KV to new pages and frees old pages.
aria: background compaction could hurt throughput — need backoff and preemption for SLOs
sam: agreed. compaction is low-priority and token-bucket limited; we also pre-scan to target only pages where live_bytes < 40% and free_runs > threshold.
devin: any interaction with FlashAttention/fused-attn batching? prefetching KV pages into GPU is time-sensitive — if alloc triggers page-split right when batch runs, we might incur syncs
sam: we added a small prefetch hint in the index: pages with sequential access get a 'prefetch_score' that the runtime uses to warm KV into device memory before the request hits GPU. This reduces stalls for large seq lengths.
aria: can you add a short graf in the RFC about controlled prefetch and how it plays w/ batching heuristics?
sam: will do. also thinking about a 'soft-evict' flag so runtime can drop older KV pages lazily if memory pressure rises during critical batches.
maya: tests needed: 1) long-running fragmentation sim 2) sudden spike workload with small allocs 3) interaction with streaming batches (flash variants).
sam: adding test plan to PR. thanks for feedback — i'll post a PR draft tomorrow with diagrams + bench artifacts. :thumbsup:
bench-bot: attaching flame snippets soon: /artifacts/1789991111/bench-flame.svg
ops-bot: logging ticket INF-4357 to track operational rollout checklist (metrics, toggles, kill-switch)
aria: cool — tag me on the PR for the prefetch section
sam: will do. end of thread.
